top_signal.title: Any advice or tips for liquidating retail inventory?
top_signal.summary: I'll try to keep this short so feel free to ask for more info or whatever questions you have.    My family and I constructed and opened a hardware store in 2023. We didn't have any experience and got way in over our heads based on bad advice. The debt load required to fund the construction and opening costs ended up north of $2M and primarily came from SBA loans. Based on projections from the international brand we were partnered with, this was supposed to be sustainable. Unfortunately the projected sales ended up being almost double our actual revenue in our best year. We fought as hard as we could to make this thing work but it was patching holes on the titanic. Don't get me wrong, we made our share of blunders, but in the end I believe it was doomed from the start.   Long story short, we've been bled completely dry and have decided to close the doors and sell. The business isn't profitable so we're essentially just selling the real estate, FF&E, and inventory. We've found a buyer for the Real Estate and FF&E, but we're now having to contend with the inventory. It's mostly hardware/home goods/garden center merchandise.    We've gotten a couple recommendations for liquidation companies (WinGate Sales Solutions for example) and they honestly rub me the wrong way. It also bugs me that almost none of these companies have any public reviews despite having pitch media with dozens and dozens of testimonials. We need to get the most out of this liquidation and I don't know
